span.label: A NAMED HYPOTHESIS GIVEN A BOUNDARY CONDITION RATHER THAN A VERDICT: `Quotation withheld.` Not confirmed, not refuted - restricted. **And the condition is a property of the STIMULUS**, where Q-787's ambiguity condition is a property of the outcome situation and Holcomb2005's is a property of the observer. Three different places a priming effect can be conditional, and a corpus that records only `X primes Y` loses all three
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE PRIME MAKES THE TASK HARDER, WHICH IS THE CASE THE STANDARD DEFINITION EXCLUDES. `Subliminally priming with a face-containing image SIGNIFICANTLY IMPAIRS the subjects' ability to perceive the emotional expression of the target-face.` Minton2017 (Q-780) quotes McNamara defining priming as `an IMPROVEMENT in performance` and then strikes the word out, because `priming can also involve a change in performance that is neutral or results in POORER performance`. **This record is the counterexample that correction needed** - a real interference effect, in a different literature, from a paper that never mentions the definitional dispute
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: IT CONTRADICTS A NAMED STUDY AND SAYS SO PLAINLY: `Quotation withheld.` And it offers the reconciling detail rather than leaving the disagreement bare - `the emotional expression of a face in a prime can be processed, AT LEAST PARTIALLY, during a 16 ms exposure`. A null and a positive on the same manipulation, with an exposure duration between them
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE CONGRUENCY EFFECT IS ITSELF CONDITIONAL, WHICH IS THE SECOND `ONLY WHEN` IN ONE PAPER: `we found that specifically the INCONGRUENCY of the pleasant prime and the angry expression of the target-face lead to worse performance ... Quotation withheld.` So the paper reports an affective congruency effect, agrees it is the known one, and then restricts it - twice qualifying a borrowed finding rather than claiming a new one
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: subliminal priming —operationalised-as→ affective primacy
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85 — THE HYPOTHESIS IS TESTED THROUGH THE PARADIGM, and the `ONLY WHEN` is inside the quote - an edge reading `subliminal priming operationalises affective primacy` without it would state the general claim the paper spent four studies restricting. Weight 0.85: the restriction is this paper's contribution, so the unqualified relation is precisely what it does not support.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: egocentric —causes→ subliminal priming
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85 — NO `effect_direction`. Vantage-point is a two-level CATEGORY (egocentric or allocentric), not a quantity, so `increases` and `reduces` are both meaningless - what the paper reports is that the two levels DIFFER, and in which direction for which target. And what this edge cannot carry is the sharpest part: the centricity effect holds `REGARDLESS of whether the prime image contained a face`, which makes it the one route here that does NOT need the affective content. That sentence never says `subliminal priming`, so it is on the `centricity` concept row instead.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
